rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Balancing redox is double-entry bookkeeping: atoms on one ledger, electrons on the other. The **oxidation-number method** equalises totals — find every number that moves, multiply until total increase equals total decrease, then mop up O with water and H with H⁺ (NEB 2023's MnO₄⁻/C₂O₄²⁻ lands on 2 : 5 : 16 → 2 : 10 : 8).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O - Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O - MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O - 2MnO₄⁻ + 5C₂O₄²⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O - Equivalent mass = formula mass / n-factor

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Balance O with H₂O and H with H⁺ — in that order:** reversing the sequence scrambles ionic equations; charge (electrons) always comes last.  ·  **Equivalent mass is reaction-specific:** K₂Cr₂O₇ is 49 as an oxidant but different in other roles — always derive n from the actual half-reaction quoted.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Acid half-reaction recipe: "O → H₂O, H → H⁺, charge → e⁻". Common products: MnO₄⁻/H⁺ → Mn²⁺ (5e), Cr₂O₇²⁻/H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ (6e), MnO₄⁻/H₂O → MnO₂ (3e). Eq masses: 31.6, 49, 52.7.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (3m): Balance the redox reaction by the ion-electron method: MnO₄⁻ + Fe²⁺ → Mn²⁺ + Fe³⁺ (acidic medium).** — **Reduction half:** MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺. Balance oxygen with water: MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O. Balance hydrogen with H⁺: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O.…  ·  **NEB 2023 (3m): Balance by the oxidation number (half-reaction) method: MnO₄⁻ + C₂O₄²⁻ + H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + CO₂ + H₂O.** — Assign numbers: Mn falls from **+7 to +2** (decrease of 5 per Mn); carbon rises from **+3 to +4** (increase of 1 per C, i.e. 2 per C₂O₄²⁻).…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Write every intermediate step of the half-reactions — examiners award marks for O, H, charge balancing separately. Finish with the charge check; stating "+17 both sides" is a visible proof line.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Both methods are the same conservation law in two costumes: electrons (or oxidation-number units) lost must equal gained. The ion-electron half-reactions reappear verbatim as electrode reactions in electrolysis and cells — learn them once, use them thrice.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Oxidation-number method: assign ONs, equalise increase = decrease, balance rest by inspection. Ion-electron: split halves, balance O→H₂O, H→H⁺, charge→e⁻, equalise electrons, add, cancel. Worked: MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O (NEB 2024); 2MnO₄⁻ + 5C₂O₄²⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O (NEB 2023).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Hydrogen sulphide scrubbers, bleaching plants and iron-and-manganese water filters all run balanced redox equations of this topic's type — the arithmetic keeps industrial chemistry lawful.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Making Electrons Balance on Paper A redox equation must balance twice: atoms **and** electrons. Two formal methods deliver this — the **oxidation-number method** (compare numbers, equalise total increase and decrease) and the **ion-electron (half-reaction) method** (split into oxidation and reduction halves, balance each, add).…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Oxidation-number method — the steps 1. Write the skeleton equation and assign oxidation numbers to every atom. 2. Identify the elements whose numbers change; note the **increase** and **decrease** per atom. 3. **Equalise** total increase = total decrease by multiplying species with suitable coefficients. 4.…  ·  ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Value to quote | |---|---|---| | **Half-reaction** | One half of a redox: oxidation or reduction alone | MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺ | | **Ion-electron method** | Balancing by adding balanced half-reactions | Electrons cancel | | **Oxidation-number method** | Balancing by equalising total ON change | Increase = decrease | |…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Verified PYQs: NEB 2024 — ion-electron balancing of MnO₄⁻/Fe²⁺; NEB 2023 — oxidation-number balancing of MnO₄⁻/C₂O₄²⁻; NEB 2021 — equivalent mass of K₂Cr₂O₇ = 49 (all solved above). NEB 2022's H₂O₂ question is answered in topic 38. Other items are NEB-style practice.  ·  "In a balanced redox equation, the total increase in oxidation numbers equals the total decrease — equivalently, electrons lost equal electrons gained."  ·  Balance FeSO₄ + KMnO₄ + H₂SO₄ → Fe₂(SO₄)₃ + K₂SO₄ + MnSO₄ + H₂O by the ion-electron method.

Balance H: 8H⁺ on the left.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **The two methods side by side** | Basis | Oxidation-number method | Ion-electron method | |---|---|---| | Principle | Total ON increase = total decrease | Electrons lost = electrons gained | | Works best for | Molecular equations | Ionic equations in acid/base | | Bookkeeping | Coefficients…  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Electrons never appear in the final answer:** they cancel when the halves are added — an equation with electrons left in it is unfinished work.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Medium changes n-factor:** KMnO₄ takes 5 electrons in acid but only 3 in neutral solution (MnO₂ product) — quote the medium with every equivalent mass.  ·  **Charge balance is the proof:** after balancing, check total charge on both sides; if it differs, an electron count is wrong.  ·  ## 7. Exam Application **Verified PYQ (NEB 2024): Balance by the ion-electron method: MnO₄⁻ + Fe²⁺ → Mn²⁺ + Fe³⁺ (acidic medium).** — Reduction half: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O (O by water, H by H⁺, charge by electrons). Oxidation half: Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Verified PYQ (NEB 2023): Balance by the oxidation number method: MnO₄⁻ + C₂O₄²⁻ + H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + CO₂ + H₂O.** — Mn falls +7 → +2 (5 per Mn); carbon rises +3 → +4 (2 per oxalate). Equalising at LCM 10: 2 MnO₄⁻ and 5 C₂O₄²⁻. Balancing O and H with water and H⁺: **2MnO₄⁻ + 5C₂O₄²⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O**.…  ·  **Verified PYQ (NEB 2021): Calculate the equivalent mass of K₂Cr₂O₇ acting as an oxidising agent in acid medium.** — In acid, dichromate accepts 6 electrons: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O (each Cr drops +6 → +3). Formula mass = 2(39) + 2(52) + 7(16) = 294. **Equivalent mass = 294/6 = 49.**  ·  **NEB-style (3m): Balance Cu + dilute HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + NO + H₂O by the oxidation-number method.** — Cu: 0 → +2 (increase 2); N in HNO₃: +5 → +2 in NO (decrease 3).
